 Canada eye Nations League glory after fantastic 2026 finale
 Ben Steiner
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 TORONTO - In a sense, the remarkable story of Canada 's historic 2026 men's national team began and ended at Toronto FC ’s BMO Field.
 On the same pitch where their record-breaking run to the FIFA World Cup Round of 16 began back with a first-ever World Cup point in June, 2026 came to a close for Canada on Monday with one last party on the shores of Lake Ontario, this time in a  4-1 win (7-3 aggregate) in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.
 Guatemala opened the scoring before Jonathan David levelled the game. Former Minnesota United striker Tani Oluwaseyi netted a brace, and ex- New England Revolution standout Tajon Buchanan added another, punching Canada’s ticket to the Nations League semifinals and the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup . 
 “We've taken steps as a team this year ... There have been times where people have complained that we're not getting enough goals, that we're not playing a good brand of football, but as you can see in this game today, we dominated from start to finish,” said Oluwaseyi postgame. 
 “For us, it's just continuing to grow as a team and taking a performance like this and being able to do it against the bigger teams, against the US, and then even from there against all the other teams around the world.”
 Tani Oluwaseyi finishes off a feed from Liam Millar🇨🇦 #CANMNT pic.twitter.com/zuvodjfJFk 
— TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 17, 2026 
 Tani time 
 Oluwaseyi’s goalscoring excellence had been a long time coming in a Canada shirt. 
 Through his 31 previous appearances entering camp, he had scored just twice. Since Friday, he scored three goals in two games, elevating his international form after scoring against English Premier League giants Liverpool in the UEFA Champions League with LaLiga’s Villarreal last month.
 “Even when he is not scoring goals, he's helping the team so much in this all-around game, but I'm very happy for him today that he was able to reward himself with two goals,” said Buchanan of Oluwaseyi, after also scoring his first goal since June 2025. 
 “Every time we come into camp, we're improving as a team, and that's the most important thing. We’re trying to take this team to new heights, and I think in 2026 we were able to do that.”
 Tani Oluwaseyi grabs his second of the night 🙌 #CANMNT pic.twitter.com/GKKRZT0Gyy 
— TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 17, 2026 
 Trophy dreams 
 Canada’s 2026 finished with plenty of marquee moments and a 7W-3L-4D record.
 From the nation’s first-ever World Cup point against Bosnia and Herzegovina to an emotional win over Qatar and Stephen Eustáquio's dramatic winner against South Africa for a run to the Round of 16, the year delivered no shortage of defining moments.
 Yet it is clear that the program is further along now than at the beginning, with head coach Jesse Marsch committed through the rest of the 2030 cycle . Now, the focus turns to searching for a first trophy since the 2000 Gold Cup, starting with the Nations League semifinal on March 25 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.
 “We put ourselves in a situation where we could go for a trophy, and we know we haven't won the Nations League, and [we] think this team is good enough,” said assistant coach Mauro Biello, who filled in Monday after head coach Jesse Marsch was sent off in the first leg.
 “If we're able to get [some of] these injured guys and all revving their engines, we're going to be able to do really good things with it.”
 Tajon Buchanan adds another for Canada to extend their aggregate lead to 6-3! #CANMNT pic.twitter.com/BFCgEeaHiQ 
— TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 17, 2026 
 For club and country 
 While Canada’s curtain closes on 2026, the trophy chases haven’t yet shuttered for Canada’s MLS talents, with each of Real Salt Lake ’s Luc de Fougerolles , Orlando City ’s Maxime Crépeau , Portland Timbers ’ Joel Waterman , LAFC 's Mathieu Choiniére , Inter Miami 's Dayne St. Clair and  Vancouver Whitecaps FC ’s Ralph Priso bound for the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. 
 Less than 72 hours after Monday’s final whistle, De Fougerolles and Crépeau will take to the pitch in Wild Card games. The others have time to focus on the Round One Best-of-3 Series.
 “Whether you play for your country or your club, you want to perform at a high level and chase the biggest goals,” said Waterman.
 “We put ourselves in a good position to go far in the playoffs, and so I'm really excited to play for that club and to be a part of that club and to play in front of the insane atmosphere too, with all those fans.”
 Even without some of the top talents available throughout the year due to injury, 2026 will be remembered as one of the most formative years for the sport in Canada. And in many ways, the next step is clear — find silverware.
